title: introduce-network-firewall-egress-assembly-and-conditional-endpoint-routing
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: provide an opinionated, auditable egress control path for private control plane deployments by combining AWS Network Firewall assemblies with conditional VPC endpoint routing and per-subnet SG mirroring. This reduces blast radius for misconfigured NAT gateways, enables customer-facing policy enforcement in regulated environments, and unblocks customers who require DPI-based egress filtering.
Summary of changes: 1) new terraform module terraform/modules/control-plane-firewall that provisions a Network Firewall assembly (firewall policy, stateful rule groups, firewall), associated route tables, and conditional route propagation to a shared egress VPC; 2) add conditional endpoint routing support in terraform/modules/vpc-endpoints so that interface endpoints can be routed to the closest AZ egress proxy when enabled; 3) subnet pool improvements: introduce deterministic tagging for controlplane-isolated-subnet pools and automatic SG mirroring (controlplane-sg -> inspection-sg) so traffic from controlplane subnets is visible to the inspection boundary; 4) helm chart: redwood-private-installer chart values updated to expose enable_network_firewall, egress_vpc_id, and endpoint_routing_mode with backward-compatible defaults; 5) migrations/upgrade: a step-by-step Terraform plan/apply sequence and a helm rollout diagram to minimize downtime; 6) integration tests and a new smoke test harness that validates route table associations and endpoint connectivity.
Checklist: [x] terraform module with unit tests and docs; [x] helm values and chart bump; [x] migration docs and step-by-step guide in docs/migrations/network-firewall.md; [x] integration CI job added to perf-canary; [x] security review sign-off.
Migration notes: This introduces a change to how control plane egress is routed when enable_network_firewall is toggled. Default behavior remains unchanged (NAT-based egress) until operators explicitly enable the new assembly. When enabling for an existing deployment follow the documented order: 1) create egress VPC and central firewall using the module in staging; 2) attach inspection subnets and ensure mirroring SGs are present; 3) enable endpoint_routing_mode=conditional and run terraform plan/apply; 4) verify with the smoke test before flipping production traffic. Rollback: helm value toggle + terraform destroy of the firewall module in reverse order; full rollback instructions included in docs.
Testing: manual end-to-end validation against a synthetic control plane in our staging AWS account, integration CI that runs endpoint connectivity checks (icmp/http), and policy enforcement tests that simulate blocked domains. Performance impact: measured <5ms additional p95 egress latency for control plane RPCs in our staging baseline.
Related: reference architecture diagram added to docs/arch/network-firewall.svg and links to customer request SUP-342.

review_comments: Harish Patel: Can we avoid modifying existing route tables by default? Suggest an opt-in flag for existing stacks.
Maya Chen: Added endpoint_routing_mode with values [none|conditional|force]; default kept at 'none' to preserve current behavior.
Evan Liu: Network Firewall policy seems permissive in staging; please tighten the default rule groups to deny-by-default and add explicit allow for required control-plane domains.
Maya Chen: Tightened rule group to deny-by-default and added allow rules for known control plane endpoints. Also added automated tests to validate policy semantics.
Sofia Martínez: Please document failure modes when the firewall is unreachable. How does the control plane degrade?
Maya Chen: Documented fail-open vs fail-closed recommendations and our chosen default (fail-open for existing customers; optional fail-closed is available behind a toggle).
release_notes: Added an optional Network Firewall-based egress assembly for control plane deployments. New Helm values: enable_network_firewall, egress_vpc_id, endpoint_routing_mode. Introduces a terraform module for centralized inspection and conditional endpoint routing. Backward compatible by default. See docs/migrations/network-firewall.md for upgrade steps.
